title: "Stage 11 – Few clusters and the multiverse"

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
**Slides.** [Open the deck at the menu](../../slides/eu-frames-full.html#/the-specification-menu){target="_blank"}, in Part 3, in its own tab, or follow it on the [slides page](slides.qmd).
:::

The last stage of the last case works the largest menu of the course, fourteen decisions and a curve of 864 specifications, and asks two questions that the earlier cases met only in part. The first is how much certainty a panel of twenty-seven countries can give, when every result is tested by standard errors clustered by country with the CR2 correction. The second is what hundreds of estimates on the same data can establish when they are not independent tests. The stage ends with the fourth case report and the choice of your project, and takes about five and a half hours.

| Work through | What you do | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| [Specification menu](../../cases/eu-frames/menu.qmd) and [Decision map](../../cases/eu-frames/map.qmd) | The fourteen decisions and the three levels into which they sort, the options that the curve of 864 keeps, and the alignment of every result with the direction of the claim; then every decision on the map, in the order in which an analyst meets it, with what each option does to the estimand statement and to the results. | 40 minutes |
| Slides, the menu in Part 3, and Task 4 in your report or working script, or [browser lab](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd#task-4-explore) Task 4 | The menu and the methods behind each of its decisions, then `try_spec()` one argument at a time, compared with `my_experiments()`. Ask once for pooled OLS (`estimator = "pooled_cl"`) to read why it is refused, and send the try that you would defend with `submit_exploration()` if you want it on the [class chart](../../cases/eu-frames/multiverse.qmd#class-results). | 40 minutes |
| Slides, [Part 4](../../slides/eu-frames-full.html#/part-4-multiverse-and-preregistration){target="_blank"} | The multiverse tutorial, the class chart against the curve of 864, the decision that carries the largest share of the variation across specifications, where the five reanalyses and the original study sit, your own placement on the curve, and the inference that a curve does and does not support. | 40 minutes |
| The preregistration block in your report, or [browser lab](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd#task-5-my-preregistration) Task 5 | Complete the block before you run anything, one option for each of the fourteen decisions, and run `prereg()`; then translate the declaration into model syntax yourself, run it, and send it with `report_result()` if you want it on the chart. | 30 minutes |
| [The statistical methods behind the course](../../companion/stats-methods.qmd), [Fixed effects](../../companion/stats-methods.qmd#sec-fe) and [Within and between](../../companion/stats-methods.qmd#sec-re), read again | The sections that stage 6 read with respondents in mind, now on the panel for which they were written. Country fixed effects against two-way fixed effects and what each comparison holds constant; why ten years of one country carry less information than ten independent observations, and the CR2 correction with its Satterthwaite degrees of freedom, the rule by which every point of the curve is classed; and the within–between model that gives each kind of variation its own slope. Under the CR2 rule the reproduced specification, the model of C6HJR on which the menu is built, has a p of 0.0504 on 9.8 degrees of freedom, so it is not significant at 5% under the test of the curve, although its conventional p is 0.0002. | 45 minutes |
| [Reading a specification curve](../../cases/eu-frames/reading-inference.qmd) | Description and inference, why 864 estimates on the same data are not 864 independent tests, what a permutation test of the whole curve would have to do, and what can be said without one. | 35 minutes |
| [The multiverse and its critics](../../companion/multiverse.qmd#sec-eu-frames), the section on the EU-frames case | The debate of stage 4 on a curve of hundreds of specifications: pruning a menu of fourteen decisions, one correct analysis on a larger curve, the fork chart, the strength of the evidence, and heterogeneity and influence. | 35 minutes |
| [Missing answers](../../companion/missingness.qmd) | What a respondent who mentions no frame at all does to a share built from mentions, the rules that the menu offers for such respondents and what each assumes, and multiple imputation against the rules set by fiat. | 30 minutes |
| Your report | Render the report with all five tasks complete, the preregistration as it stood before the run and the result beneath it. This is the fourth case report. | 20 minutes |
| [The projects](stage-12.qmd#the-projects), on the page of stage 12 | Read the list and choose one case and one question beyond its claim. Stage 12 sets up version control before you write the preregistration, so that a dated commit fixes the declaration before anything runs. | 20 minutes |
| Optional: [The items behind the scales](../../companion/measurement.qmd), [Weights](../../companion/weighting.qmd), [The individual level](../../companion/individual-level.qmd) and [Simulation as a method](../../companion/simulation.qmd) | The battery of items behind the outcomes of this case, its dimensions and its reliability, in the sections of the measurement module that come before the immigration-and-trust case; the weights of the cells and the population weight as another estimand, in the sections of the weights module that come before that case; the claim fitted at the level of respondents, where the original author (OA) fitted it, on the simulated person-level dataset of the course, which is validated against the real respondents; and data with a known recipe, in which a method can be checked against an answer known in advance. Each supports a project on this case. | as you like |

**Shortcuts.** If stage 6 left fixed effects and few clusters clear, skip the second reading of the statistics module and keep only its section on [standard errors with few clusters](../../companion/stats-methods.qmd#sec-inference).

**By the end of the stage** you have your declared result placed among the 864 specifications of the curve, the fourth case report rendered, a sentence on what the CR2 test by country changes for the reproduced specification, and the question of your project chosen.
